test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In January 2022, Kriti paid an EMI, which was 22% of her monthly salary. She spent the remaining salary on shopping of groceries and clothes in the ratio 7 ∶ 5. She spent Rs. 18,200 on shopping of clothes. If, in February 2022, her salary increased by 16%, then what was her salary (in Rs.) in February?
solution:
**Given**

Kriti paid an EMI, which was 22% of her monthly salary

She spent the remaining salary on shopping of groceries and clothes in the ratio 7 ∶ 5.

She spent Rs. 18,200 on shopping of clothes.

**Formula used:**

Income = expenditure + savings

**Calculation**

Let the income be x.

The amount given to Emi = 22x/100

= 11x/50

Remaining amount = 39x/50

Expense on clothing = 5/12 × 39x/50

= 13x/40

⇒ 13x/40 = 18,200

⇒ x = 1400 × 40

⇒ x = 56000

If, in February 2022, her salary increased by 16%:

⇒ 56000 × 116/100

⇒ 64960

**Her salary (in Rs.) in ****February is 64960**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the income be x.

⇒ x × 78/100 × 5/12 = 18200

⇒ x = 56000

Salary in February = 56000 × 116/100 = 64960.
